title: Husky and lint-staged
description: Set up Husky and lint-staged to automate linting and formatting on staged files only.

data.text: Husky is a Git hooks manager that stores hook scripts in your repository, making them shareable across your team. lint-staged runs linters and formatters only on staged files, keeping pre-commit checks fast regardless of repository size.
Husky v9 (the current version) uses a .husky/ directory for hooks. Initialize it with npx husky init, which creates the directory and a default pre-commit hook.

data.title: Initialize Husky in a project
data.code:
# Install Husky as a dev dependency
npm install --save-dev husky

# Initialize the .husky/ directory
npx husky init

# This creates:
# .husky/
# .husky/.gitignore
# .husky/pre-commit

# The default pre-commit hook contains:
# npm test

# You can edit or replace it:
npx husky add .husky/pre-commit "npx lint-staged"

git add .husky/
git commit -m "chore: add Husky hooks"

data.text: lint-staged runs commands on staged files only. It accepts a glob pattern for file matching and a list of commands to run. This means a large repository with 10,000 files only lints the 5 files in your commit.

data.title: lint-staged with separate config file
lint-staged is much faster than full lint
data.text: Running eslint on a large repository can take 30+ seconds. lint-staged runs it on only the staged files, typically completing in under a second. This makes pre-commit hooks practical.

items: **Hook not running**: Ensure .husky/pre-commit is executable: chmod +x .husky/pre-commit
**lint-staged not found**: Use npx lint-staged in the hook, not the binary path
**Changes not staged**: lint-staged automatically stages fixed files, but verify with git status
**Slow on first run**: lint-staged caches file lists; performance improves after the first commit

items.question: Does lint-staged modify my files permanently?
items.answer: Only if the linter/formatter changes them. lint-staged runs the commands, stages the modified files, and the changes become part of the commit. Review the changes before committing.

items.question: Can I use lint-staged without Husky?
items.answer: Yes. lint-staged works independently with any Git hooks manager or even a manual pre-commit hook.

items.question: How do I skip lint-staged for a specific commit?
items.answer: Use git commit --no-verify to skip all hooks including lint-staged. Some teams add a [skip lint] tag in the commit message to skip selectively.

items.question: Can lint-staged run on non-JS projects?
items.answer: Yes. lint-staged works with any command-line tool. Use it for shellcheck, black (Python), dotnet format (C#), or any linter that supports file arguments.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Husky manages Git hooks from a committed .husky/ directory
lint-staged runs commands only on staged files for speed
lint-staged automatically stages fixed files after running
Use chmod +x to ensure hooks are executable
